items.title: NYSE Selects Avalanche for Tokenized US Equities Settlement
points: NYSE selected Avalanche (a public layer-1 blockchain network) exclusively for a new 24/7 tokenized US equities settlement platform, targeting Q4 launch pending regulatory approval.
Platform will enable instant settlement using stablecoin-based funding, citing Avalanche's transaction speed, throughput, and compliance capabilities.
BlackRock's BUIDL fund reached $486.5M on Avalanche in Q3; Apollo, Franklin, and Janus Henderson are also building on the network, signaling major institutional adoption of a public blockchain.

items.title: Warren to Scrutinize Prediction Markets and Crypto as Senate Banking Chair
points: Senator Elizabeth Warren takes the Senate Banking Committee gavel in January and plans to scrutinize prediction markets, Trump family crypto businesses, memecoin operations, and World Liberty Financial's UAE connections.
Her office has already pressed prediction-market platforms Polymarket and Kalshi on insider trading and election betting, and demanded document preservation from Trump-affiliated crypto operations.

items.title: MARA Holdings Q3 Results and Bitcoin Treasury Standing
points: MARA Holdings posted a $634.4M Q3 net profit, driven by $885M in digital asset gains, despite a 35% revenue decline.
The company cut debt by 37% and is shifting strategy toward execution over infrastructure expansion.
MARA's corporate bitcoin treasury ranking dropped to fifth (passed by Strive); it now holds 850,364 BTC (~4.05% of the 21M total supply) at an average cost basis of $75,456 per coin.

items.title: Securitize Acquires River One to Enter Asset-Backed Finance Market
points: Securitize acquired River One to enter the $6.1 trillion asset-backed finance market.
Q3 results showed $5B in average tokenized assets (assets represented as blockchain tokens), up 39% year-over-year, and $4.3B in transaction volume, up 20% year-over-year.

items.title: Vitalik Buterin Reframes Ethereum as a Store-of-Value Asset
points: Vitalik Buterin is repositioning Ethereum's value proposition toward store-of-value stability rather than fee-burning mechanics (EIP-1559, a rule that destroys a portion of transaction fees to reduce supply), treating burn as incidental even if it stays below 10% of breakeven long-term.
He points to protocol-level 'CROPS' properties—immutability and resistance to capture by external forces—as the long-term value driver, especially relevant during AI disruption.
This reframes ETH from a yield-focused asset to a stability-focused reserve asset, prioritizing decentralization and capture-resistance over fee-burning optimization.

items.title: Goldman, Citi, and Santander Fund a Bank-Backed Stablecoin
points: Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, and Banco Santander are jointly funding development of a bank-issued stablecoin (a cryptocurrency pegged to a stable value like the US dollar), signaling major institutional acceptance of digital assets.
The partnership combines a US investment bank, a US commercial bank, and a major European lender, suggesting the project targets global cross-border payment capabilities.
A bank-backed stablecoin addresses longstanding volatility and counterparty-risk concerns, offering a more stable alternative to decentralized stablecoins for institutional use.

The move could accelerate blockchain-based settlement adoption, reduce friction in international transfers (which traditionally take days via multiple intermediaries), and position banks to compete with crypto-native stablecoins and central bank digital currencies (CBDCs, digital currencies issued directly by central banks).
Involvement of three systemically important financial institutions suggests regulatory pathways for institutional stablecoins are becoming clearer.

headlines: Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, and Banco Santander are jointly funding a bank-backed stablecoin (a cryptocurrency pegged to a stable value like the U.S. dollar), signaling major institutional acceptance of digital assets in traditional finance.

sections.title: Major Banks Launch Stablecoin Initiative
points: Three global financial institutions—Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, and Banco Santander—are co-funding the development of a bank-issued stablecoin, marking a significant milestone in mainstream financial adoption of blockchain technology.
The partnership combines the reach of a U.S. investment bank, a U.S. commercial bank, and a major European lender, suggesting the project aims for global cross-border payment capabilities.

A stablecoin backed by established banks addresses longstanding concerns about cryptocurrency volatility and counterparty risk, potentially creating a more stable alternative to decentralized stablecoins for institutional use.

sections.title: Why This Matters for Markets
points: Bank-issued stablecoins could accelerate adoption of blockchain-based settlement and payments, reducing friction in international transfers that traditionally take days and involve multiple intermediaries.
This move positions traditional banks to compete with crypto-native stablecoin projects and central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), while capturing value in digital asset ecosystems.
The involvement of three systemically important financial institutions suggests regulatory pathways for institutional stablecoins are becoming clearer.
